record.paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
record.original_question: Determine how to achieve stable bipedal walking on unknown, uneven ground, where the terrain is not flat and may vary significantly. This includes understanding the mechanics, modeling choices, and feedback design needed for robust locomotion when the robot must handle irregular contact conditions rather than the flat-ground case emphasized in the paper.

evidence.quote: This tutorial emphasized walking on flat ground. Much less is known about the problem of bipedal walking on unknown, uneven ground.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3D bipedal robot modeled as a hybrid dynamical system consisting of:

(i) Continuous single-support (and possibly double-support) phases governed by Lagrangian dynamics
   D(q) q̈ + C(q, q̇) q̇ + G(q) = B u + J(q)^T λ,
where q ∈ Q ⊂ R^n is the configuration, u ∈ R^m is the control input, λ are ground-reaction forces enforcing unilateral contact constraints (foot non-penetration, friction-cone, and zero-moment conditions);

(ii) Discrete impact maps modeling foot touchdown,
   (q^+, q̇^+) = Δ(q^-, q̇^-),
which reset velocities under a rigid plastic-impact assumption.

Let the terrain be described by an unknown function h : R^2 → R giving the ground height, with bounded slope and curvature but otherwise not known a priori to the controller. The robot has no advance map of h; at each step the location and orientation of the support surface beneath the swing foot is revealed only at (or shortly before) impact.

Problem. Construct a feedback control law u = κ(q, q̇, y), where y is online sensory information available to the robot (e.g., joint encoders, IMU, contact sensing, possibly proprioceptive estimation of local terrain), together with a choice of reference / virtual-constraint or gait-library structure, such that the closed-loop hybrid system admits a forward-invariant set of states from which the robot executes an infinite sequence of steps without falling, for every admissible terrain function h in a prescribed class H of uneven grounds (characterized by uniform bounds on slope, step height, and friction). Equivalently, exhibit a provably stable walking strategy on unknown uneven terrain in the above class, or establish fundamental obstructions to its existence.
artifact.status_search_result: Stable 3D bipedal walking over unknown uneven terrain remains an active and largely open research problem. Substantial partial progress exists (e.g., gait libraries, hybrid zero dynamics extensions, rough-terrain MPC, and learning-based controllers demonstrated on robots like Cassie and ATLAS), but no general control framework with rigorous stability guarantees over arbitrary unknown uneven terrain has been established.

status_evidence.title: Cassie rough-terrain walking via reinforcement learning
status_evidence.snippet: Learning-based controllers achieve robust walking on varied terrains in simulation and hardware, but without formal stability proofs over a general class of unknown grounds.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work yields empirical robustness on uneven terrain but not full theoretical guarantees.

status_evidence.title: Feedback Control of Dynamic Bipedal Robot Locomotion (Westervelt et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference establishing hybrid zero dynamics methodology primarily for flat ground.
status_evidence.claim: The foundational stability theory is developed for flat ground; extension to unknown uneven terrain remains open.
